candidates.plaintext: The students use a small application to read their grades and comments. A teacher can enter a grade after each lesson. The application keeps the records in a database. The team must protect the private comments before a person can copy the database. A secret key changes the readable text into ciphertext. The same key changes the ciphertext back into readable text. Keep the key separate from the data. Use a new nonce for each message. Check the authentication tag before you use a comment. Reject a comment if the check fails. Encryption helps protect stored comments, but the application must also check who can read each record.
